questions.question_text: By writing each number correct to 1 significant figure, find an estimate for (3\sqrt{987} \times (16.3 + 1.91^2)) / \sqrt{9.12}. You must show your working.
Explain why your answer to part (a) is greater than the actual answer.
Solve the equation: 4 log 3 - 3 log 4 = log x - 5 log 2
Solve the equation: 4 \sin x + 3 = 1 for 0\deg \le x \le 360\deg
Make x the subject of the formula: a = \sqrt{(x-1)/x}
Find the mean geography mark from the table of marks.
Find the mean history mark from the table of marks.
Find the equation of the regression line for y in terms of x.
Estimate the history mark when the geography mark is 51.
Write down the transformation that is the inverse of P.
Write down the transformation that is the inverse of Q.
Describe fully the single transformation equivalent to P followed by Q.
Find the next term and the nth term in the sequence: 27, 20, 13, 6, -1, ...
Find the next term and the nth term in the sequence: 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64, ...
Calculate an estimate of the mean mark from the frequency table.
Complete the cumulative frequency table.
On the grid below, draw a cumulative frequency curve.
Use your graph in part (c) to find an estimate for the median mark.
Use your graph in part (c) to find an estimate for the interquartile range.
Use your graph in part (c) to find the minimum mark for a candidate to obtain a grade A, given that 15% of students gain a grade A.
On the diagram, sketch the graph of y = f(x) where f(x) = (6x+11)/(2x-3), for values of x between x = -4 and x = 6.
Write down the equations of the asymptotes.
Write down the co-ordinates of the points where the graph crosses the axes.
Solve the inequality: x < (6x+11)/(2x-3)
Freddo leaves Manchester at 0705 and arrives in Cambridge at 1050. The distance is 300km. Calculate his average speed.
After the meeting Freddo drives back to Manchester. His average speed is 5% more than his average speed driving to Cambridge. He leaves Cambridge at 1745. Find the time Freddo arrives in Manchester.
Freddo's car uses fuel at the rate of 8.1km per litre. Fuel costs £1.45 per litre. Find the total cost of fuel for Freddo's journey from Manchester to Cambridge and back to Manchester.
A coat costs $100. The price is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. Find the new price of the coat.
A chair costs $1000. The price is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. Find the new price of the chair.
A car costs $10 000. The price is increased by x% and then decreased by x%. Find an expression, in terms of x, for the new price of the car.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Three balls are chosen at random without replacement. Find the probability that all are red.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Three balls are chosen at random without replacement. Find the probability of two red and one blue.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Three balls are chosen at random without replacement. Find the probability of at least one of each colour.
This experiment is to be carried out 1680 times. Find the expected frequency of 3 red balls being chosen.
A is the point (2, 6) and C is the point (5, 4). The equation of line AB is y + 4x = 14 and BC is y = x - 1. Find the co-ordinates of B.
M is the midpoint of AC. Find the co-ordinates of M.
Find the equation of the line BM.
The point D lies on the line BM. The co-ordinates of D are (k, k+9). Find the value of k.
In the diagram, ABC is a straight line and BFED is a rectangle. Find BC.
Show that angle DBC = 34.7°, correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the perimeter of the quadrilateral ACDE.
Find the area of the quadrilateral ACDE.
On the diagram, sketch the graph of y = f(x) where f(x) = (100 / 2^x) - 10, for 0 <= x <= 5.
Write down the x co-ordinate of the point where the graph crosses the x-axis.
Write down the range of f(x).
Solve the equation: (100 / 2^x) - 10 = 20
Describe fully the single transformation that maps the graph of y = 100 / 2^x onto the graph of y = (100 / 2^x) - 10.
A fraction P has denominator x. The numerator of the fraction is 3 less than the denominator. Write down fraction P in terms of x.
The numerator and the denominator of fraction P are each increased by 3 to give fraction Q. Write down fraction Q in terms of x.
Given Q - P = 9/40, write down an equation in x and show that it simplifies to x^2 + 3x - 40 = 0.
Solve the equation x^2 + 3x - 40 = 0.
Write down the original fraction, P.
Solve the inequality: 5 / (2x - 1) < 3
Solve the inequality: log(2^x) > 10
